item.title: Patrick Clancy sits down with 60 Minutes
item.description: Patrick Clancy spoke with 60 Minutes this week. Shanelle Kaul has a preview of the story, which airs Sunday.

item.title: Details on Ed Sheeran tour as all acts quit after Macklemore dropped for pro-Palestine comments
item.description: Ed Sheeran is facing intense public backlash after rapper Macklemore, who was set to open his upcoming tour dates, was dropped from the production over pro-Palestine comments. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports and Alex Suskind, news director at online music magazine Pitchfork, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: House passes Russia sanctions bill, overcoming Democratic opposition
item.description: The bill was championed by GOP Sen. Lindsey Graham, who suddenly died after announcing a deal had been reached with the White House to move forward.

item.title: Federal agencies spent $9.5 billion on salary costs for administrative leave in 2025
item.description: A new report from the Government Accountability Office shows federal agencies spent $9.5 billion on administrative leave costs in 2025, an increase spurred by the DOGE push to cut down the federal workforce. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has more.

item.title: Coast Guard and FBI boarded tankers due to cyberattacks. How big is the risk?
item.description: U.S. Coast Guard personnel and FBI agents boarded two Texas-bound energy tankers last month after cyberattacks struck the vessels while they were traveling toward the United States, according to U.S. officials.

item.title: Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time since 2023
item.description: The Fed increased its benchmark rate by 0.25 percentage points to battle resurgent inflation driven by soaring energy prices.

item.title: When an intruder invaded a golden retriever's home, he just tried to play
item.description: A golden retriever got his big chance to be a guard dog, but instead of guarding, Nash tried to play with the intruder. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Video shows first responders rushing to flame-engulfed motel, saving lives
item.description: Newly released video shows fire ripping through a Florida motel this weekend and first responders rushing into the danger. Cristian Benavides spoke with two of them.

item.title: North Carolina GOP Senate nominee Michael Whatley reacts to farmer's criticism of tariffs, gas costs
item.description: President Trump is traveling to North Carolina to stump for Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley. CBS News chief White House correspondent Nancy Cordes spoke with Whatley ahead of the president's appearance.

item.title: Video shows Coast Guard, FBI boarding oil vessel suspected of being hacked by Iran
item.description: The FBI and the Coast Guard are investigating a giant oil tanker on its way to Texas that may have been taken over by a cyberattack. Iranian state media claims hackers had control of the ship's propellers, raising concern that these giant vessels could be used as weapons. Nicole Sganga reports.

item.title: Companies illegally selling unapproved Eli Lily weight loss drug Retatrutide online
item.description: Retatrutide, an experimental weight loss drug still undergoing clinical trials at Eli Lily, is being marketed online and illegally sold to U.S. clients, a CBS News investigation found. CBS News investigative reporter and producer Daniel Gilbert has the story.

item.title: Fed raises interest rates, a sign of concern about rising prices: "Inflation is too high"
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years on Wednesday, a sign of concern about rising prices. Meanwhile, the cost of diesel fuel hit a new record on Wednesday, for the eighth day in a row. Nancy Cordes reports on rising prices and Kelly O'Grady has more details on the Fed's decision.

item.title: Kamala Harris to campaign with El-Sayed in Michigan
item.description: CBS News has confirmed that former Vice President Kamala Harris will campaign with Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. Political strategists Ofirah Yheskel and Greta Joynes join "The Takeout" with analysis.

item.title: FBI investigating potential father-son serial killer duo
item.description: FBI agents are investigating two potential serial killers, a father and his son, possibly involved in the killings of at least five women. Jericka Duncan reports.

item.title: Judge Judy's son, Adam Levy, previews new show "Adam's Law"
item.description: Judge Judy has been a staple of daytime TV for 30 years, but now televised courts are becoming a family affair with her son, Adam Levy, picking up the gavel and donning the robe for "Adam's Law." Judge Levy joins CBS News to preview the new show.

item.title: House passes late Sen. Lindsey Graham's Russia sanctions bill, sending it to Trump's desk
item.description: The House on Wednesday evening passed a Russia sanctions bill championed by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham. CBS News congressional reporter Taurean Small has the latest.

item.title: Details on news helicopter crash in LA, killing 3
item.description: A news helicopter went down in Los Angeles on Tuesday night while the reporter aboard was covering a fatal bus accident. Two NBC LA employees were killed in the crash, along with another person on the ground. Carter Evans reports.

item.title: The races to watch with balance of power in Congress up for grabs
item.description: CBS News' director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto breaks down the congressional races to watch ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: Eradicate Hate president says nonprofit is "needing to get creative" amid federal grant cuts
item.description: The Eradicate Hate Global Summit is underway in Pittsburgh, with a focus on preventing future tragedies by ending hate-fueled violence. The group's president, Brette Steele, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Trump says interest rates should be at "1% or less" as Fed hikes them for first time since 2023
item.description: The Federal Reserve boosted interest rates for the first time since July 2023 on Wednesday. CBS News' Richard Escobedo and Natalie Brand have the details.

item.title: House passes bill to shield Americans from data center energy costs
item.description: The vote comes as lawmakers face increasing pressure to respond to the data center boom driven by the AI race.

item.title: Florida Democratic governor hopeful David Jolly says politics are at a "1974 post-Watergate moment"
item.description: Democrats are bullish this election cycle, even eyeing the governor's mansion in President Trump's adopted home state of Florida. The nominee, David Jolly, faces an uphill battle as Democrats haven't won a statewide race in the Sunshine State since 2018. Jolly joins "The Takeout" to discuss his campaign.

item.title: Georgia execution delayed for hearing under new law that may reduce sentence
item.description: A Georgia judge has put an execution on hold to allow time for a hearing on whether the sentence should be reduced under a new state law that lets victims of abuse have their sentences reconsidered.

item.title: Coast Guard, FBI boarded Texas-bound oil tanker to investigate cyberattack
item.description: The U.S. has so far not attributed the potential breach to a specific actor, but Iranian state media amplified the story in the weeks following the attack.

item.title: Foreign actor breached network of Texas-bound oil tanker, federal authorities confirm
item.description: Federal authorities have confirmed that a foreign actor compromised the network of two oil tankers that were heading towards Texas in August. CBS News homeland security correspondent Nicole Sganga has the details.

item.title: Why the Fed hiked interest rates this month
item.description: The Federal Reserve changed course and raised interest rates Wednesday for the first time since 2023. The rate hike will be an increase of 0.25 percentage points, bringing its target range to between 3.75% and 4%. Greg Robb, MarketWatch senior reporter and economics editor, joins CBS News with more.

item.title: ISIS-K member sentenced to 20 years in prison in case tied to Kabul bombing
item.description: An Islamic State group member was sentenced to 20 years in prison for aiding the terrorist organization that took credit for a suicide bombing that killed 13 U.S. service members and about 160 Afghans at a Kabul airport.

item.title: NASA spacecraft discovers moon crater bigger than Roman Colosseum
item.description: Scientists have discovered a crater on the moon that's bigger than the Roman Colosseum, the result of a powerful impact two years ago.

item.title: 9/16: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Federal Reserve unanimously votes to raise interest rates; President Trump stumping for GOP Senate nominee Michael Whatley in North Carolina.

item.title: Sunday: Patrick Clancy in his own words, only on 60 Minutes
item.description: This Sunday on 60 Minutes, Patrick Clancy talks about his grief, his memories of his children, and the baseless conspiracy theories that flooded social media since his ex-wife's murder trial.
